questions.prompt: All of the following bones are involved in the formation of the posterior nasal aperture (choana) except...?
options: Vomer
Palatine
Sphenoid
Maxilla
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The posterior choana is bounded by vomer, palatine and sphenoid; maxilla does not form its boundary.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 1; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following arteries branches from the maxillary artery, which is a branch of the external carotid artery?
options: Sphenopalatine
Anterior Ethmoidal
Posterior Ethmoidal
Superior labial
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Sphenopalatine is a terminal branch of the maxillary artery. The ethmoidal arteries arise from ophthalmic, and superior labial from facial.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 2; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options is correct?
options: The ethmoidal bulla is located below the inferior concha.
The maxillary sinus opens into the Semilunar hiatus.
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the middle meatus.
The middle ethmoidal air cells open into the superior meatus.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The maxillary sinus drains into the middle meatus through the semilunar hiatus. Nasolacrimal drainage is to the inferior meatus; the ethmoidal bulla is in the middle meatus.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 3; source page 2.

questions.prompt: All of the following structures are adjacent to the medial surface of the right lung except...?
options: Arch of azygos vein
Thoracic duct
Superior vena cava
Inferior vena cava
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The named right-lung mediastinal relations include the azygos arch and the venae cavae. The thoracic duct is not a direct named right-lung impression.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 4; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options is a characteristic of the parietal pleura?
options: It is innervated by the sympathetic nerve.
It penetrates into the deep fissures.
The inferior border of the parietal pleura at the midclavicular line is at the level of the eighth rib.
The pulmonary ligament is derived from the visceral pleura.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Parietal pleura reaches the eighth rib at the midclavicular line. It has somatic sensory innervation and does not enter the deep lung fissures.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 5; source page 2.

questions.prompt: All of the following options are correct except...?
options: The right main bronchus is wider than the left main bronchus.
The right main bronchus is shorter than the left main bronchus.
The left main bronchus is further from the midline compared to the right main bronchus.
The left main bronchus divides before entering the hilum of the right lung.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The left main bronchus enters the left, not the right, lung. The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical. The source's incorrect laterality is preserved.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 6; source page 3.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options is incorrect?
options: The upper border of the quadrangular membrane forms the aryepiglottic fold.
The aryepiglottic fold plays a role in the formation of the laryngeal inlet.
The false vocal fold is attached anteriorly to the arytenoid cartilage.
The upper border of the cricothyroid membrane (conus elasticus) forms the true vocal cords.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The vestibular/false fold attaches anteriorly to thyroid cartilage and posteriorly to arytenoid; C reverses this relationship.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 7; source page 3.

questions.prompt: All of the following are correct about the internal laryngeal nerve, except:
options: It pierces the thyrohyoid membrane.
It has muscular branches.
It supplies sensation to the laryngeal mucosa above the true vocal cords.
This nerve is one of the two terminal branches of the superior laryngeal nerve.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: In the standard course description, internal laryngeal is the sensory branch above the vocal folds. External laryngeal supplies cricothyroid; recurrent laryngeal supplies the other intrinsic muscles.

questions.prompt: The lung bud originates from which of the following parts?
options: Endoderm
Visceral mesoderm
From the sixth pharyngeal arch
Foregut
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Withheld: A identifies the epithelial germ layer and D the anatomical origin; the lung bud is a ventral foregut endodermal outgrowth, so both can answer this unspecific stem. No supplied key resolves the mixed categories.

questions.prompt: In the structure of the olfactory epithelium, which of the following is correct?
options: It contains bipolar sensory neurons.
Bowman's serous glands cause lubrication of the duct.
The axons of olfactory neurons are in the lamina propria.
Olfactory cells have basal cilia.
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Withheld: both A (bipolar sensory neurons) and C (their axons in the lamina propria) are correct. The source asks for a single answer and provides no key; these alternatives are retained, not silently rewritten.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 10; source page 3.

questions.prompt: In the structure of the respiratory epithelium, which of the following is correct?
options: Kulchitsky cells have apical granules.
Brush cells have apical microvilli.
Goblet cells contain lipoprotein.
Columnar cells have apical nuclei.
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Brush cells have apical microvilli. Kulchitsky cells have basal dense-core granules, and goblet-cell secretory material is mucin rather than lipoprotein.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 11; source page 4.

questions.prompt: In the histological structure of the trachea:
options: The epithelial cells lack granules.
The C-shaped hyaline cartilage is under the adventitia.
Mucous glands in the submucosa produce a watery serous secretion.
The ends of the tracheal cartilage are covered by the trachealis skeletal muscle.
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: B is the anatomical statement supported by the source: C-shaped hyaline cartilage lies deep to the adventitia, between it and submucosa. Trachealis is smooth muscle; mucous and serous secretions should not be interchanged.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 12; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Regarding the histological structure of the lung, which of the following is correct?
options: The respiratory bronchiole has cartilaginous plates.
The terminal bronchiole has seromucous glands.
In the terminal bronchiole, the height of the epithelium is greater.
Clara cells appear in the terminal bronchiole.
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Withheld: D is true (club/Clara cells occur in terminal bronchioles), but C omits the structure against which epithelial height is being compared. Terminal epithelium is taller than distal respiratory/alveolar lining but lower than proximal bronchi, so the incomplete comparison prevents a unique audited answer.

questions.prompt: If in a patient with pneumonia the diffusing capacity of CO2 is 300 ml/min/mmHg, what will be the diffusing capacity of oxygen in this person (in ml/min/mmHg)?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Using the course's approximate CO2:O2 diffusing-capacity ratio of 20:1, DLO2 = 300/20 = 15 mL/min/mmHg.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 14; source page 4.

questions.prompt: In which generation of the lower airways is the resistance highest?
options: Left and right main bronchi
Tenth generation bronchi
Fifteenth generation terminal bronchioles
The last generation of respiratory bronchioles
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A is the best listed answer in the course's aggregate-resistance comparison: proximal bronchi have fewer parallel paths than the much more numerous distal bronchioles. This does not assert that main bronchi are the precise maximum in every airway-generation model; medium-sized bronchi are often emphasized.

questions.prompt: What is the difference in intra-alveolar pressure (in cm H2O) at the end of a normal inspiration compared to the beginning?
options: zero
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At the beginning and end of normal inspiration, airflow is momentarily zero and alveolar pressure equals atmospheric pressure. The endpoint difference is zero; -1 cm H2O describes pressure during inward flow.

questions.prompt: By filling a lung with saline solution, what change occurs in the elastic forces of the lung compared to an air-filled lung?
options: The elastic forces increase.
The elastic forces do not change.
Only the elastic force due to elastin and collagen is preserved and functional.
The distending pressures required to overcome the elastic forces increase.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Saline removes the air-liquid interface and its surface-tension recoil; tissue recoil from elastin and collagen remains. The bold A line is a formatting inconsistency, not a systematic supplied answer key.

questions.prompt: What effect does alkalosis have on the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve?
options: It decreases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, causing a shift to the right.
It increases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, causing a shift to the left.
It decreases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, causing a shift to the left.
It increases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, causing a shift to the right.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Alkalosis reduces H+ and shifts the oxyhemoglobin curve left, increasing oxygen affinity.

questions.prompt: Clinically, the measurement of pulmonary wedge pressure is performed to estimate the pressure in which part?
options: Right atrial pressure
Pulmonary artery systolic pressure
Pulmonary artery diastolic pressure
Left atrial pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Wedge pressure is used as an indirect estimate of left atrial/downstream pulmonary venous pressure under suitable conditions; it is not a direct measurement of pulmonary arterial systolic pressure.

questions.prompt: In the dynamics of fluid exchange across pulmonary capillaries in a healthy person, which Starling force has the greatest contribution towards the exit of fluid from the capillary to the interstitial space?
options: Colloid osmotic pressure of the interstitial fluid
Capillary hydrostatic pressure
Negative pressure of the interstitial space
Plasma colloid osmotic pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the course's illustrative normal pulmonary Starling-force model, outward interstitial oncotic pressure is about 14 mmHg, exceeding the 7 mmHg capillary hydrostatic and 8 mmHg negative interstitial contributions. Plasma oncotic pressure acts inward.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 20; source page 5.

questions.prompt: In a healthy, standing person, the value of which factor is lower at the base of the lung than at its apex?
options: Alveolar ventilation rate
Blood flow rate
Ventilation to perfusion ratio (V/Q)
Capillary hydrostatic pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Both ventilation and perfusion increase toward the base, but perfusion increases more, making V/Q lower at the base than the apex.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 21; source page 6.

questions.prompt: If the ventilation/perfusion ratio becomes zero, what will happen to the partial pressure of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveoli?
options: The partial pressure of oxygen will reach 149 mmHg.
The partial pressure of carbon dioxide will reach 45 mmHg.
The partial pressure of oxygen will become zero.
The partial pressure of carbon dioxide will become zero.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: With V/Q = 0, perfusion continues without ventilation. Alveolar gas approaches mixed venous values: PCO2 about 45 and PO2 about 40 mmHg in the standard reference model.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 22; source page 6.

questions.prompt: What effect does the weakening of the pneumotaxic center in the pons have on the breathing pattern?
options: The respiratory rate increases.
The apneustic center becomes stronger.
Breathing stops.
The duration of the ramp signal produced in the DRG increases.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Weaker pontine inspiratory switch-off allows the inspiratory ramp to last longer. The direct tested effect is prolonged inspiration, not creation of a stronger separate center.

questions.prompt: Where is the partial pressure of oxygen the highest?
options: Arterial blood
Alveolar air
Expired air
Anatomic dead space
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At the end of normal inspiration the conducting/anatomic dead-space gas resembles humidified inspired air, with higher PO2 than mixed expired or alveolar air and arterial blood. The option is interpreted in that conventional respiratory-cycle comparison.

questions.prompt: Which of the following factors causes a decrease in lung compliance?
options: Increased accumulation of elastin and collagen in the lung parenchyma.
Increased amount of surfactant in the alveoli.
Emphysema
Sympathetic stimulation
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: More fibrous elastin/collagen framework increases elastic recoil and reduces compliance. Surfactant and loss of recoil in emphysema have the opposite tendency.

questions.prompt: Which of the following factors does not change during exercise?
options: Pulmonary blood flow rate
Pulmonary ventilation rate
Partial pressure of oxygen in alveolar air
Blood flow velocity through pulmonary capillaries
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: During ordinary steady exercise in a healthy person, ventilation increases with oxygen uptake and generally maintains alveolar oxygen pressure near resting values. This is an approximate regulated value, not a claim covering maximal exercise or lung disease.

questions.prompt: If in a patient with anemia the amount of hemoglobin in the blood is 10 g/dL and its oxygen saturation is 90%, approximately how many milliliters of oxygen will be present per deciliter of this person's blood, bound to hemoglobin?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Hemoglobin-bound O2 = 10 g/dL × 1.34 mL/g × 0.90 = 12.06 mL/dL, approximately 12. The calculation excludes dissolved oxygen as requested.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 27; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which process does NOT occur during the stimulation of carotid chemoreceptors due to a decrease in oxygen pressure?
options: Entry of calcium into the glomus cell
Release of acetylcholine from the glomus cell
Depolarization
Increased potassium efflux from the glomus cell
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Hypoxia inhibits oxygen-sensitive K+ conductance: potassium efflux decreases, followed by depolarization, Ca2+ entry and transmitter release. Increased potassium efflux is the opposite.

evidence: Respiratory System - 29-question digital paper (September 2025 filename); printed question 28; source page 7.

questions.prompt: The magnitude of the safety factor against the development of pulmonary edema is determined by which factors?
options: Plasma colloid osmotic pressure and capillary hydrostatic pressure
Interstitial fluid colloid osmotic pressure and capillary hydrostatic pressure
Plasma colloid osmotic pressure and interstitial fluid colloid osmotic pressure
Plasma colloid osmotic pressure and negative pressure of the interstitial space
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In the traditional acute hydrostatic-edema safety-margin comparison, normal plasma oncotic pressure (~28 mmHg) is compared with pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure (~7 mmHg), giving about 21 mmHg. This is a simplified textbook margin, not an individual clinical threshold; drainage and barrier integrity also matter.
